rationale: Shep asked for race-day splits off the course profile in a clubmate's 2025 Cheltenham file (she ran 1:21:02, so her per-km elevation deltas map the course at close to his goal pace). This proposes no change to any session — only to the race entry's notes, so the plan carries the checkpoint times on the day rather than only the pace band. The target stays 1:22:00 rather than 1:21, for three reasons: the model predicts 1:22:23; 1:21 needs 3:51/km from the gun, which is a decision made at the start and not recoverable if it is wrong; and a well-run 1:22 that finishes strongly lands 1:21:34, so the faster time is available as an outcome without being gambled on as a plan. Splits are gradient-adjusted from the course profile rather than flat, so effort stays even: slightly slower on the climbs at km 6, 12 and especially 20 (+11m, the clubmate's slowest split of the day by seven seconds), slightly quicker on the drops. The one hard rule is km 1: it falls about 5m and was her fastest split of the race at 3:38, which is his current 10K pace. Capping it at 3:56 costs three seconds against even pacing and removes the single biggest risk on the day — she went out 7 sec/km quicker than her own average and lost 2:25 in the back half. Nothing here changes the taper or any session before Sunday.
